about: Planted in setup.sql / gen_workload.py. Row counts in bundle/ybm_reltuples.csv are measured counts x100 (build.sh SCALE). 'engine_match' is what yb-model.py must emit; 'engine_absent' is what it must not emit (a finding, review text, or point_query_contains: a pattern the engine must not model as a point lookup); 'judge' is what a grader looks for in a free-text review. 'traps' are things a review should NOT claim.

defects.pattern: SELECT metric, label, value FROM counters WHERE tenant_id = .. AND device_id = .. AND grp = .. AND bucket = ..
defects.judge: The read binds bucket after metric and label, which it leaves unbound: DocDB seeks under every (metric, label) of the device and group. A key with bucket before metric (as counters_by_bucket has) reads one contiguous range. Re-keying is the user's decision; the other order costs reads that bind metric across buckets.

traps.judge: Do not call the named-metric read (an OR of conjunctions) a point lookup or list it as already sound: it returns one row per arm.
The bucket-first table serves the same read without a gap; no key-gap finding on it.
Do not claim the gap read scans every row of the device: DocDB skip-scans, so rows scanned stay close to rows returned; the cost is seeks.
